subject: Remediation plan kickoff and evidence collection for Ethan Park
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Early concerns — Ethan Park (eng) performance trend and next steps

Neha / Monica —

I wanted to flag that Ethan's Q3 velocity and quality metrics have trended below team expectations for multiple sprints. I attached a quick export (2026-09-daily-metrics-ethan.csv) showing missed deliverables and regression-related bugs tied to his PRs.

Before we escalate formally, I want to align on a remediation approach that:
- gives clear expectations and measurable goals,
- sets evidence collection that is defensible, and
- minimizes legal risk while supporting improvement.

Can HR and Legal advise on a PIP timeline we typically use for individual contributors in Eng (30/45/60 day options), plus any mandatory steps (e.g., prior written warnings) we must document? I can draft the manager-facing plan if you confirm the template.

Attachments: previous-performance-notes.pdf

Thanks,
Markus
Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early concerns — Ethan Park (eng) performance trend and next steps

Thanks Markus —

I read the CSV and the notes. My suggested next steps:
1) 30-day focused remediation period to start as soon as we meet with Ethan (shorter window given product timelines).
2) Manager-owned success criteria (deliver X features, reduce bug reopen rate by Y%). I can draft the precise metrics and daily check-ins.
3) Collect the supporting evidence you referenced (PR comment history, failing test logs, missed sprint commitments). Please drop anything else into the Drive link and I'll consolidate.

HR / Legal, can you confirm: is a prior written warning required in this case, or can we initiate a PIP as the first formal remediation given documented coaching conversations? Also: any mandatory language we need in the initial notice?

I will prepare a first-draft plan (manager view) and circulate for redline.

—Neha
People Ops Business Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Remediation plan draft and template

Neha / Markus —

Thanks for pulling the data. I've uploaded a standard PIP template with two timeline options (30 / 60 days) to the Drive and attached a DOCX here (draft-pip-outcome-options.docx). The template includes:
- objective success criteria,
- meeting cadence (weekly 30-mins),
- coaching resources, and
- a clear escalation path if expectations aren't met.

Notes / HR guidance:
- We typically require documentation of prior informal coaching attempts. The "previous-performance-notes.pdf" you attached will help.
- If we proceed without a formal written warning, we should ensure the initial meeting is framed as a "focused improvement plan" with follow-up notes to be acknowledged by the employee.
- Keep evidence collection limited to role-related artifacts (PRs, sprint board, test logs) — avoid subjective peer commentary unless anonymized.

I recommend we also consider bringing in an external performance coach (Mira Alston at PeopleOps) to run a 1:1 session mid-plan if we think it could help. Mira is ok with quick engagements; I can make an intro.

Attachments: draft-pip-outcome-options.docx
Drive: https://drive.reddwood.example.com/teams/eng/perf-packs/ethan-2026-Q3

Monica
Senior HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Legal checklist for PIP initiation — Ethan Park

Team —

I've reviewed the draft template. A few legal redlines and clarifying questions:
1) Language: avoid implying guaranteed outcomes. Replace phrasing like "will be terminated if" with "may be subject to further action, up to and including termination, if expectations are not met."
2) Evidence retention: keep copies of all PIP communication in the employee's personnel file. Ensure access logs for Drive artifacts are captured in case of later disputes.
3) Disparate impact check: confirm that similar performance thresholds were applied across the team and that there are no protected-class concerns. Markus, can you confirm comp/role/level parity?
4) Privacy: if we loop external coach Mira, obtain signed consent from the employee before sharing any performance logs.

I attached a short redlined checklist in the Drive and added suggested language for the initial notice. If HR prefers, I can produce a final "employee-facing" version for you to send.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Employment
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Focused improvement kickoff — meeting invite and plan (please review)

Ethan —

As discussed in our 1:1s this quarter, we've seen several areas where your output has not matched expectations for your role. To give you a clear path and support to improve, we'd like to start a focused improvement plan. This is intended to be constructive and time-boxed.

Please review the attached manager plan and the expected success criteria before our kickoff meeting on Oct 1 at 11:00am PT (calendar invite sent). Key points:
- Duration: 30 days (Oct 1 — Oct 31)
- Success criteria (examples): ship Feature A commit with test coverage and follow-up bug rate below 5%; complete two pairing sessions per week; reduce PR reopen rate to <= 2 per sprint.
- Weekly check-ins with me; HR will join the initial and final review.

Attachments: draft-pip-outcome-options.docx, 2026-09-daily-metrics-ethan.csv

If you have concerns about fairness or would like a coach involved, please tell us in the kickoff so we can coordinate (Mira Alston, external coach, is an optional resource).
